history.dynasty: None documented for the temple itself; the Davangere region was Nolambavadi under the Chalukyas, then passed through Pandyas, Hoysalas, Vijayanagara kings, Palegar Nayaks, Marathas, Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan, and finally the Mysore Wodeyars
history.period: Shrine origins attributed to the 18th century (weakly sourced); a stone brought from Dugatti/Duggatti village was installed and worshipped as Durga Devi about 200 years ago; the present temple was built in 1932
history.summary: Sri Durgambika Temple is one of the biggest and most popular temples in Davangere city, standing in old Davangere (Halepet, Shivajinagar - the surrounding area is locally called 'Devara Hatti'). Tradition holds that around 200 years ago a stone was brought from Dugatti (Duggatti) village and installed here for worship as Durga Devi; in 1932 this shrine was converted into the present Durgambika Temple, built in Dravidian style with outer walls sculpted with Durga, Ganesha and other deities. The presiding deity Durgambika is known locally as Durgamma, Durgavva and Durgambika. Every Tuesday and Friday the temple committee arranges special puja, and once in two years a grand 10-day fair in March-April draws devotees from Chitradurga, Haveri, Bellary, Dharwad, Shimoga and beyond. The settlement area around the temple has a long history - part of the Nolambavadi province in Chalukya times, changing hands through Pandyas, Hoysalas, Vijayanagara rulers, Palegar Nayaks, Marathas, Hyder Ali/Tipu Sultan, and the Mysore kings, under whom Davangere grew into a prosperous textile centre. CSV town/state (Davangere, Karnataka) are correct; the temple's specific address is SKP Road, Kotval Pet, Shivaji Nagar, Davangere 577001.

name: Sri Durgambika Temple
town: Davangere (old Davangere / Halepet, Shivajinagar; neighbourhood locally called 'Devara Hatti')
town_description: Davangere (Davanagere) is a major city in central Karnataka, historically a prosperous cotton-textile centre under the Mysore Wodeyars (called the 'Manchester of Karnataka') and famous for its benne (butter) dosa. The Durgambika temple stands in the old part of the city at SKP Road, Kotval Pet, Shivaji Nagar (Davangere 577001), about 1 km from the railway station and city bus stand.

travel.airport: Kempegowda International Airport, Bengaluru - about 273 km (per Velpu).
travel.road: City Bus Stand about 1.1 km; the temple is on SKP Road, Kotval Pet, Shivaji Nagar, in old Davangere (Halepet area).

visitor_information.best_time: September to February (winter season) is the best time to visit; the biennial jatra in March-April is the grandest but most crowded.
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM - 8:00 PM daily (per Velpu). Special pujas on Tuesdays and Fridays. Dress code is enforced: men in shirt-trouser/dhoti/pyjama with upper cloth, women in saree/half-saree/chudidar; shorts, sleeveless tops and similar dress are not allowed (verify on visit).
